title: Meta Platforms Stock: Is it a Steal of a Deal at $650?
detail:
Meta Platforms Stock: Is it a Steal of a Deal at $650?
David Jagielski, CPA, The Motley Fool

META
NVDA
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

This year has been a volatile one for social media giant Meta Platforms (NASDAQ:META). It has hit highs of nearly $780, and its lows have been around $520. It's a vast range, and it demonstrates just how polarizing a stock this can be. On the one hand, it's a growth machine. On the other, it's also extremely aggressive when pursuing new growth opportunities, and thus, high capital spending can weigh on investors' minds.

Right now, the market is feeling bearish on Meta's stock again. Its latest quarterly results weren't impressive enough to justify sending the stock to an even higher valuation. But with it down close to 20% from its high, could it be a steal of a deal right now, while it trades at around $650?

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 16x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

Image source: The Motley Fool.

What has spooked investors?

Before buying a stock on a dip, it's important to understand why it's down to determine whether this is temporary adversity weighing on the stock or longer-lasting problems to worry about.

While Meta's business performed well in the third quarter, which ended on Sept. 30, with sales rising 26% and beating expectations, it appears that, once again, concerns about high spending are keeping growth investors away.

During the quarter, the company's free cash flow went negative, with $2.1 billion leaving the business, as its capital expenditures were higher than the cash flow that it generated from its day-to-day operating activities. The company has been investing heavily in artificial intelligence (AI), and the worry is that the payoff may not be there.

In September, the company revealed its personal AI agent, Muse, which aims to help people with day-to-day tasks. It's a key part of the company's AI strategy, but whether consumers will trust an AI associated with a company that doesn't have the greatest track record for data privacy is certainly questionable.

The stock looks cheap, but I wouldn't call it a steal

Meta's stock is trading at a forward price-to-earnings multiple of 18, which is based on analyst projections. That's an attractive-looking price tag for a top tech giant.

However, the company has faced adversity in recent years, coming under pressure from lawmakers about protecting children on its platforms and overall data privacy. There's some concerning long-term risk here, which I believe warrants a greater discount for the stock than where it trades at right now. That's why, as cheap as Meta's stock may look right now, I wouldn't rush to buy it.

title: Why Meta Platforms Stock Rallied on Monday
detail:
Why Meta Platforms Stock Rallied on Monday
Danny Vena, CPA, The Motley Fool
Mon, November 9, 2026 at 12:23 PM CST 3 min read
META
NVDA
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Shares of Meta Platforms (NASDAQ:META) rallied on Monday, gaining as much as 5.6%. As of 12:47 p.m. ET, the stock was still up 5.1%.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 16x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

The broader market rebound no doubt contributed to the move, but bullish commentary from a Wall Street analyst helped push the social media and artificial intelligence (AI) specialist higher.

Image source: The Motley Fool.

Bullish take

JPMorgan analyst Doug Anmuth added Meta Platforms to the investment bank's Analyst Focus List, calling it a preferred internet stock. The analyst cited the robust growth in the company's AI-powered ad sales and the potential represented by its Muse AI models. Anmuth maintained its overweight (buy) rating and $940 price target on the stock. For those keeping score at home, that represents potential upside of 54% compared to Friday's closing price.

A quick look at the company's recent results supports the analyst's bullish position. In the third quarter, Meta delivered revenue that grew 26% year over year to $64.6 billion. Moreover, diluted earnings per share (EPS) rose 265% to $3.83. Excluding a one-time charge to settle litigation, Meta's EPS of $7.40 would have risen sevenfold.

Furthermore, the company's potential to monetize its Muse AI personal AI agent shouldn't be overlooked. The Muse app had been downloaded more than 5 million times within three weeks of its release -- outpacing ChatGPT, which took 56 days to reach that benchmark. Muse has since surpassed 10.9 million downloads, according to digital intelligence and market analytics company Sensor Tower. Moreover, it remains one of the top-ranked apps on both the Android and Apple app stores.

Muse's popularity has the potential to turn into profit. Beyond its limited free tier, Meta charges $20 per month for its Power tier and $100 per month for its Maximum tier. While estimates vary, Muse could generate incremental revenue of $27 billion by 2030, according to Citigroup. The AI agent is increasingly helping users search, compare, and complete transactions online.

To be clear, the company still faces ongoing litigation as several cases wind their way through the courts. That said, much of that risk is already baked into Meta's stock price, and at less than 22 times earnings, the potential upside far outweighs the risk.

The fourth-quarter guide implies 13% to 18% sequential revenue growth, and adding back the litigation charge lifts third-quarter operating income to about $22.9 billion, a margin near 35%. Price per ad rising faster than impressions suggests AI targeting is improving monetization. The next test is fourth-quarter revenue landing inside the guide while 2027 capex plans stay disciplined.

Key Takeaways

Eaton stock is down 23% in the past month. Meta Platforms' spending plans and the Democrats' midterm sweep hit AI power-equipment stocks across the board, Vertiv and GE Vernova included.

The selloff erased the gain from a record third quarter, in which Eaton's Electrical backlog grew 46% and it raised its 2026 organic growth outlook to 13-15%.

RBC Capital raised its target to $539 after the report, but to get there investors would have to pay a higher forward P/E than at any point in five years.

At 22x forward earnings, below its 25x five-year average, Eaton looks like a buy, and its fourth-quarter report in February will show whether data-center orders are holding up.

Eaton (ETN:NYSE) stock is down 23% in the month to Nov. 6, erasing the gain from its best quarter ever.

It went down with the rest of the AI power trade. Vertiv (VRT:NYSE) lost 28% and GE Vernova (GEV:NYSE) 25% over the same stretch. They were hit first by spending plans from Meta Platforms (META:NASDAQ), then by the Democrats' midterm sweep. Eaton is still up 7% in 2026.

A record quarter, and a higher outlook

Eaton reported before the open on Nov. 3, Election Day, and set records almost across the board:

Sales rose 28% to $8.9 billion.

Adjusted EPS was $3.68, against roughly $3.55 expected.

Electrical backlog grew 46% from a year earlier, with rolling 12-month organic orders up 39% in Electrical Americas and 51% in Electrical Global.

Management raised its 2026 organic growth outlook to 13-15%, with adjusted EPS of $13.70-$13.80.

Analysts expect earnings to keep climbing, to $16.28 a share in 2027 from $12.07 in 2025:

Eaton (ETN): normalized EPS, actual and consensus estimates, $ per share, fiscal 2024-2029 (TIKR)

Even the low end of the new guide tops the $13.67 consensus for 2026, so nothing here points to estimate cuts. The stock jumped 7% that day, then lost almost 10% the next.

TIKR tracks 28 analysts on Eaton. How many say "Buy"?

See the full breakdown of Buy, Hold, and Sell ratings on Eaton, along with Wall Street's revenue and earnings estimates, all in one place. More than 500,000 investors use TIKR to research stocks like this one. See Eaton's Analyst Ratings

Meta and the midterms sank the whole group

The trouble started with Meta's third-quarter report after the close on Oct. 21. Its free cash flow turned negative, and it raised the low end of its 2026 capex range, to $135-145 billion. That means more data-center spending, but investors worried how hyperscalers will pay for it. Meta is down 17% over the month, and Eaton fell 6% on Oct. 22 with the rest of the group.

Then Democrats won both chambers of Congress, and Texas' governor-elect, Gina Hinojosa, has pledged to halt new data-center approvals until lawmakers pass new rules. That revived fears that US data-center construction could slow. Eaton fell 10% on Nov. 4, and the next day an AI-led market rout took the S&P 500 down more than 4% and Eaton down another 7%.

Oklo (NYSE: OKLO) develops small modular reactors, or SMRs. These nuclear facilities are faster to build and have lower upfront capital needs than conventionally sized nuclear power plants.

To sustain growth, the AI industry needs a massive amount of new energy to power its data center infrastructure. This desperate need for more energy from big-budget AI companies has led to a surge in interest in SMR developers, including Oklo.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 16x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

Already, Meta Platforms has agreed to a 1.2 GW SMR system. Pre-construction is scheduled to begin in 2027. Full-scale construction is expected to start either in late 2028 or early 2029. Will the start of construction for Meta's SMR system help Oklo's stock price?

There's one major risk Oklo investors should understand.

Could Meta's SMR project with Oklo be delayed?

AI adoption continues to surge. The challenge is building enough data centers to meet that growth in demand. In recent weeks, AI stocks have corrected sharply as the pace and scale of the data center build-out come under question.

"AI demand remains strong," stresses research from Barclays. "What the market is questioning is funding, as hyperscalers keep lifting capex while free cash flow evaporates ."

Image source: Getty Images

As financing for AI projects comes under scrutiny, expect Oklo's cost of capital to rise. Already, a weak share price combined with a lack of profitability will likely force painful shareholder dilution. Any further deterioration in AI sentiment could force delays to its SMR project with Meta. That's particularly true, given that Oklo has not yet been approved by the U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission to build a commercial SMR.

Note that even under Oklo's own timeline guidance, the project would not begin generating electricity until 2030 at the earliest, with full capacity not reached until 2034. Don't expect any meaningful updates regarding Oklo's deal with Meta anytime soon. And given current market sentiment, investors may be waiting even longer than expected.
